newsitem.title: USA: U.S. municipal bond activity at 3-yr high - report.
newsitem.headline: U.S. municipal bond activity at 3-yr high - report.

text.p: Long-term municipal new issuance activity climbed to a three-year high of $180 billion in 1996, a 14.6 percent rise over 1995, Securities Data Co said in a report issued on Tuesday.
The 1996 new money volume came to $123.4 billion, exceeded only by volume in 1985, when issuers rushed deals to market before tax law changes took effect.
For the second straight year, Goldman Sachs & Co ranked as the top lead underwriter of long-term municipal new issues, having lead-managed 284 issues totaling $20 billion.
Smith Barney Inc ranked second with $18.6 billion, while Merrill Lynch & Co ranked third with $16 billion.

Orrick Herrington & Sutcliffe was the top bond counsel of 1996, having served as bond counsel on 312 long-term municipal new issues totaling $15.5 billion. Hawkins Delafield & Wood ranked second, serving as bond counsel on $11.3 billion, while Brown & Wood placed third with $10.2 billion.
Public Financial Management Inc was the top-ranked municipal financial adviser, advising on 262 issues worth nearly $11 billion.
Acting as an adviser on 59 issues placed Public Resources Advisory Group second with a volume of $9.3 billion. First Southwest Co ranked third with $5.5 billion.
Securities Data Co, part of Boston-based Thomson Financial Services, is a leading provider of financing and merger information.
